pages.title: Welcome to Your Learning Journey
pages.excerpt: A warm introduction for students of Shaiq Muhammad — how to use this platform, encyclopedias, and video lessons.
pages.body:
Assalamu alaikum and welcome.

This learning platform is built for the students of **Shaiq Muhammad**. Here you will find written lessons, video explanations, and the Encyclopedia of Quran and Encyclopedia of Hadith — integrated on this site.

## How to study here

1. Open **Encyclopedia of Quran** and **Encyclopedia of Hadith** from Home or the navigation — they stay on shaiqmuhammad.com.
2. Watch the latest **video lessons** for explanations you can revisit anytime.
3. Read the **learning pages** for notes, summaries, and reflection prompts.

May Allah make your study beneficial and lasting. Ameen.

pages.title: Daily Practice Tips
pages.excerpt: Simple habits for consistent Quran and Hadith study — short sessions, review, and sincerity.
pages.body:
Consistency beats intensity. A short, sincere daily practice is better than long sessions once a week.

## Suggested routine

- **Morning:** Recite or review a short portion with meaning from the Encyclopedia of Quran.
- **Evening:** Read one Hadith with its explanation from the Encyclopedia of Hadith.
- **Weekly:** Rewatch one video lesson and write three takeaways in your notebook.

## Remember

Seek knowledge with humility, ask questions kindly, and apply what you learn. Your teacher is here to guide you — use the portal Login when you need school communications or class materials.

pages.title: The Strong Believer (Hadith)
pages.excerpt: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ. احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ. وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَيْءٌ فَلَا تَقُلْ: لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا، وَلَكِنْ قُلْ: قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ، فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ».
pages.body:
## The Strong Believer

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ. احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ. وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَيْءٌ فَلَا تَقُلْ: لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا، وَلَكِنْ قُلْ: قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ، فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ».

*صحيح مسلم، 2664.* 

# English meaning

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught that a strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, although there is goodness in both. Seek what benefits you, ask Allah for help, and do not give up. If something difficult happens, do not keep saying, “If only I had done this or that.” Instead, accept Allah’s decree.

## What Makes a Believer Strong?

A strong believer has faith in Allah and tries to do what is right. Strength is not only about being physically strong. It takes strength to pray, tell the truth, help someone, and try again after a mistake. The hadith reminds us that there is goodness in every believer, so we should encourage others as we grow.

## Why Should We Be Careful with “If Only”?

Imagine that you worked hard for a test but did not get the mark you wanted. You might keep thinking, “If only I had changed that answer!” These thoughts cannot change what happened. Repeating them may make you feel more upset and stop you from moving forward.

The hadith does not tell us to ignore our mistakes. We can learn from them: “Next time, I will revise earlier and ask my teacher for help.” Learning from the past is useful. Staying trapped in regret is not.

## قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ

**English transliteration:** *Qadarullāhi wa mā shā’a fa‘al.*

**English translation:** “Allah has decreed, and He does what He wills.”

These words remind us that Allah knows what has happened, even when we do not understand it. Saying them helps us accept a difficult result and find the courage to continue. We can feel disappointed, learn a lesson, and still trust Allah.

The order of the hadith is important: **make an effort, ask Allah for help, and keep trying.** Then, when the result comes, trust Allah’s decree. A strong believer does their best and does not lose hope.

pages.title: The Truly Bankrupt
pages.excerpt: When we hear the word **“bankrupt,”** we usually think of someone who has lost all their money. However, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us about a more serious loss: arriving on the Day of Judgment with good deeds, then losing them because we have harmed other people.
pages.body:
## The Truly Bankrupt

When we hear the word “bankrupt,” we usually think of someone who has lost all their money. However, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us about a more serious loss: arriving on the Day of Judgment with good deeds, then losing them because we have harmed other people.

**The Hadith in Arabic**

عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ:

«أَتَدْرُونَ مَا الْمُفْلِسُ؟»

قَالُوا: الْمُفْلِسُ فِينَا مَنْ لَا دِرْهَمَ لَهُ وَلَا مَتَاعَ.

فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ الْمُفْلِسَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ بِصَلَاةٍ وَصِيَامٍ وَزَكَاةٍ، وَيَأْتِي قَدْ شَتَمَ هَذَا، وَقَذَفَ هَذَا، وَأَكَلَ مَالَ هَذَا، وَسَفَكَ دَمَ هَذَا، وَضَرَبَ هَذَا، فَيُعْطَى هَذَا مِنْ حَسَنَاتِهِ، وَهَذَا مِنْ حَسَنَاتِهِ، فَإِنْ فَنِيَتْ حَسَنَاتُهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْضَى مَا عَلَيْهِ، أُخِذَ مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ فَطُرِحَتْ عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ طُرِحَ فِي النَّارِ».

**رواه مسلم، حديث رقم ٢٥٨١.**

**English Translation of the Meaning**

Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“Do you know who the bankrupt person is?”

They replied, “The bankrupt person among us is someone who has neither money nor possessions.”

He said:

“The bankrupt person from my Ummah will come on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakah, but will also come having insulted one person, slandered another, unlawfully taken another’s wealth, shed another’s blood and struck another. One will be given some of his good deeds, and another will be given some of his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before what he owes has been settled, some of their sins will be taken and placed upon him. Then he will be thrown into the Fire.”

**Source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2581.** *The English text above is a translation of the meaning.* 

**What Does This Hadith Teach Us?**

This hadith teaches us that worship and good character belong together. Prayer, fasting and zakah are essential acts of worship, and we must also respect the rights of others. Insulting people, making false accusations, stealing and hurting others are serious wrongs for which a person will be held accountable.

On the Day of Judgment, the people who were harmed will receive justice. The wrongdoer’s good deeds will be given to them. If those deeds run out before the wrongs are settled, the wrongdoer will carry some of their sins. This is why the Prophet ﷺ described that person as truly bankrupt. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

**Putting the Lesson into Practice**

At school, we can apply this message through our daily choices. We can speak politely, avoid name-calling, tell the truth about others and ask permission before using their belongings. When we feel angry, we can pause and choose a calm response instead of hurting someone with our words or actions.

For example, a student may pray regularly but also laugh at a classmate or spread an untrue story about them. This hadith reminds us to take such behaviour seriously and change it. If we have harmed someone, we should stop, sincerely seek Allah’s forgiveness and try to repair the harm—such as returning something we took or correcting a false statement.

Our choices affect other people. Before speaking or acting, we can ask ourselves: **“Is this fair? Is it kind? Does it respect this person’s rights?”** Through worship, honesty and kindness, we learn to become Muslims whose behaviour reflects their faith.

pages.title: The Congregational Prayer
pages.excerpt:
عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ:

**«صَلَاةُ الْجَمَاعَةِ تَفْضُلُ صَلَاةَ الْفَذِّ بِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً».**
pages.body:
# The Congregational Prayer

**The Hadith in Arabic**

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ:

**«صَلَاةُ الْجَمَاعَةِ تَفْضُلُ صَلَاةَ الْفَذِّ بِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً».**

**English translation**

Abdullah ibn Umar رضي الله عنهما reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

**“Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than prayer offered alone.”**

*Source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 645.* 

**What Is Congregational Prayer?**

Congregational prayer, or *Salat al-Jama‘ah*, means praying together with other Muslims under the leadership of an **imam**. The worshippers follow the imam’s movements during the prayer. They bow and prostrate after him and stand in straight rows. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught Muslims to follow the imam and straighten their rows. 

**Understanding the Reward**

This hadith teaches us the great value of praying together. Congregational prayer has a reward twenty-seven degrees greater than praying alone. It is often explained as being **twenty-seven times better**. This encourages Muslims to make an effort to join others in prayer. 

The reward reminds us that prayer deserves our time and attention. When we prepare for prayer and join the congregation, we put worship at the centre of our day.

**What Can We Learn from Praying Together?**

Congregational prayer brings Muslims together. People of different ages and backgrounds stand beside one another, facing the same direction and worshipping Allah. This can strengthen friendship and remind us to treat others with respect.

Following the imam also helps us practise patience and discipline. We pay attention, wait for his movements and avoid rushing ahead. These habits can help us become more thoughtful in our daily lives.

**How Should We Behave?**

We should arrive calmly, prepare properly for prayer and respect the people around us. During the prayer, we should focus on worship, avoid distracting others and follow the imam carefully.

Imagine praying beside a friend. Instead of talking or playing, you both stand quietly and concentrate. You are helping one another take prayer seriously.

The hadith encourages us to appreciate the blessing of worshipping together. Congregational prayer gives us an opportunity to seek Allah’s reward while practising unity, patience and respect.

teacher.name: Shaiq Muhammad
teacher.title: Islamic Education - B Teacher
teacher.bio:
With 16 years and 10 months of teaching experience, I bring deep subject knowledge and a passion for making Islamic Education meaningful to primary learners. I have taught Islamic Education B in Dubai since 2012 and have been at Raffles International School since August 2017. Earlier, I taught Qur’an and Islamic Studies at Eaalim Institute in the UK.

My qualifications include an M.Ed, an M.A. in Islamic Studies, a seven-year Arabic-medium Islamic Studies diploma, hifz of the Qur’an, and the NPQLT (Leading Teaching). Alongside classroom teaching, I create animated and AI-assisted Islamic videos, use educational technology, and share resources through shaiqmuhammad.com and @almudarris_ins. My goal is to help pupils build Islamic knowledge, practise good adab, and apply what they learn in everyday life.
